meta.title: Keel — conflict diagnostics demo
meta.author: dknauss
meta.description: Keel's rolling main build beside Disable Comments, Classic Editor and Disable XML-RPC from wordpress.org, plus one stand-in host must-use plugin. Opens on the Dashboard notice; Site Health names each overlap and the setting that is not taking effect.

steps.data:
<?php
/**
 * Plugin Name: Host revision limit (Keel demo stand-in)
 * Description: Playground-only. Stands in for the must-use code a managed host ships to cap post revisions. Keel lists it in Site Health and never raises a notice about it.
 */

defined( 'ABSPATH' ) || exit;

/**
 * A host cap of five revisions per post.
 *
 * Must-use plugins load before ordinary ones, so at the same priority this runs
 * before Keel's revision limit, and Keel's setting (10 by default) is the one
 * WordPress keeps. The filter registry cannot show that ordering as a problem
 * or as harmless, which is why Keel reports must-use code for information only.
 *
 * @param int     $num  Revisions to keep.
 * @param WP_Post $post Post being revised.
 * @return int
 */
function keel_demo_host_revision_limit( $num, $post ) {
	unset( $num, $post );
	return 5;
}
add_filter( 'wp_revisions_to_keep', 'keel_demo_host_revision_limit', 10, 2 );

steps.code:
<?php
/**
 * Keel conflict-diagnostics demo: put each plugin in the configuration its own
 * settings screen would save. Runs once, as a blueprint runPHP step.
 */

require '/wordpress/wp-load.php';

// Disable Comments 2.9: "Everywhere" mode, as its settings screen saves it.
// db_version must match the plugin's DB_VERSION (8), or its upgrade routine
// rewrites remove_everywhere from a legacy key on the next load.
update_option(
	'disable_comments_options',
	array(
		'remove_everywhere'        => true,
		'disabled_post_types'      => array( 'post', 'page', 'attachment' ),
		'extra_post_types'         => array(),
		'remove_xmlrpc_comments'   => 0,
		'remove_rest_API_comments' => 0,
		'show_existing_comments'   => false,
		'settings_saved'           => true,
		'db_version'               => 8,
	)
);

// Classic Editor 1.7: "Allow users to switch editors: Yes". That registers its
// named choose_editor() callback; the default registers only __return_false.
update_option( 'classic-editor-replace', 'classic' );
update_option( 'classic-editor-allow-users', 'allow' );

// Keel: turn on the two settings these plugins contest. Force Classic Editor
// meets Classic Editor; allowing XML-RPC remote publishing meets Disable XML-RPC,
// which switches the whole endpoint off behind Keel's back.
$keel                                   = (array) get_option( 'keel_settings', array() );
$keel['force_classic_editor']           = 'yes';
$keel['block_xmlrpc_endpoint']          = 'no';
$keel['xmlrpc_allow_remote_publishing'] = 'yes';
update_option( 'keel_settings', $keel );

// Keep the Dashboard on Keel's notice rather than core's welcome banner.
update_user_meta( 1, 'show_welcome_panel', 0 );

steps.code:
<?php
/**
 * Keel conflict-diagnostics demo: let WordPress run the contested filters once,
 * the way real traffic would, so Keel's passive observers have a result to read.
 *
 * Nothing here calls apply_filters() on a policy hook. Rendering a post asks
 * comments_open() and pings_open(); a request to xmlrpc.php builds the server
 * class, whose constructor asks xmlrpc_enabled. Keel records any setting whose
 * final value differs from what it configured, for an hour.
 */

require '/wordpress/wp-load.php';

$keel_demo_posts = get_posts( array( 'numberposts' => 1 ) );
if ( $keel_demo_posts ) {
	comments_open( $keel_demo_posts[0] );
	pings_open( $keel_demo_posts[0] );
}

require_once ABSPATH . WPINC . '/class-IXR.php';
require_once ABSPATH . WPINC . '/class-wp-xmlrpc-server.php';
$keel_demo_class = apply_filters( 'wp_xmlrpc_server_class', 'wp_xmlrpc_server' );
new $keel_demo_class();
